title: vector-bridge tiled Q/K batching and rope rematerialization for lower-latency attention
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: reduce tail latency for medium-length sequences (128-1024) on multi-model serving by combining tiled Q/K micro-batching with a lightweight 'vector-bridge' rematerialization for rotary/rope state. This PR introduces a runtime-attention path that trades negligible peak memory for consistently lower p95 latency when continuous batching is active and KV cache occupancy is moderate.

What changed (high level): introduced a new attention execution path (vector-bridge) that: 1) tiles Q/K into fixed-size micro-tiles to better utilize SIMT on Ampere+ GPUs, 2) applies a compact rematerialization for rotary/rope phase factors to avoid storing large precomputed tensors in the KV cache, and 3) adds a scheduler hint so continuous-batcher can preferentially group compatible sequence-length requests into the same micro-batch.

Design notes: the vector-bridge is not a wholesale replacement for existing fused attn kernels. It is registered as a selectable kernel and chosen by the kernel-selector when (a) sequence length distribution matches tiled thresholds, (b) model metadata lists rope/rotary usage, and (c) the container has >= 2 concurrent streams. The rematerialization computes per-head sin/cos on-the-fly using a compact 1D table + linear interpolation for frequencies that fall between table entries; we validated numerical parity within 1e-5 for typical rotary implementations.

Implementation summary: single PR that touches the runtime, kernel registry, scheduler, and a lightweight CUDA microkernel: commits include a microkernel implementation (vector_bridge_attn.cu), a kernel selector heuristic (kernel_selector.cpp), scheduler hint plumbing (continuous_batcher.cpp), updates to the KV cache layout to hold a compact rope token descriptor (kv_cache.h), and tests/bench harness updates. A new unprivileged integration test drives mixed sequence workloads and asserts latency and correctness.

Benchmarks (representative): on p4d-like instance, BPE tokenizer workloads: - median latency: -8% vs current best fused kernel, - p95 latency: -18%, - throughput at 99ms SLO: +12% effective throughput. Memory: peak GPU working set increased by ~3-6% depending on batch packing. Bench harness and raw data included under test/bench/vector-bridge/bench-2026-02-17.log.

Compatibility & rollout: kernel is opt-in via a runtime feature flag (--enable-vector-bridge). Default kernel selector will only pick it for models that opted-in via model metadata (model.yaml: runtime-kernels: [vector-bridge]) to avoid surprise behavior. We included a canary rollout plan in the PR checklist.

Testing & CI: unit + integration + small-scale GPU smoke tests included. Long-running perf suite executed in CI as a separate gated job.

Rollback plan: revert selector registration if any correctness/regression is observed; fallback to fused-attn or flashbridge kernels automatically if numerical checks fail at runtime.

Checklist: - [x] Kernel implementation and tests - [x] Kernel selector heuristic - [x] Scheduler hint + continuous-batcher integration - [x] Model metadata opt-in - [x] Benchmarks and logs attached - [x] Docs snippet for operators guide

Related: links to linear tickets: ENG-4821, ENG-5073.

Notes: this PR focuses on medium sequence workloads; large sequence (>4096) still prefer the tiled long-attn path and small (<64) prefer scalar-fused path.

release_notes: Add new optional 'vector-bridge' attention kernel: reduces p95 latency for medium-length sequences via tiled Q/K micro-batching and on-the-fly rope rematerialization. Opt-in via model metadata or runtime flag. (opt-in, no breaking changes)
notes_for_ops: Enable via --enable-vector-bridge at runtime or set model.yaml runtime-kernels: [vector-bridge]. Initial canary: enable on 5% of Dedicated pools in region us-west-2, monitor p95/throughput for 24h.
enduser_impact: None by default. Opt-in kernel only affects models that include 'vector-bridge' in model metadata or when the runtime flag is set. Expected improvement for workloads with mixed sequence lengths (128-1024).
